input.input: text(await tools.exec_command({cmd:"top -b -d 2 -n 3 -w 180 | head -85","sandbox_permissions":"require_escalated","justification":"May I inspect the host WSL process table outside the sandbox to identify CPU consumers?","max_output_tokens":4500}));

content.text:
Currently, WSL is **about 97% idle**—there’s no CPU hog running.

The activity is spread across your open development sessions:

| Process | Instances | CPU combined* |
|---|---:|---:|
| Codex | 15 | 17.5% |
| Claude | 15 | 9.0% |
| Zellij | 20 | 8.8% |
| Lazygit | 15 | 8.5% |

*100% means one CPU core; WSL has 20 available.*

The busiest individual processes were Codex in `.dotfiles` (6.5%) and its Zellij session (4.5%). Lazygit briefly spiked to 19%, then settled.

If Windows is showing high CPU for WSL, it wasn’t sustained during this sample. Nothing was stopped or changed.
